data.title: CATL Opens Türkiye's First NING SERVICE Experience Center in Istanbul
data.description:
ISTANBUL, Türkiye, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CATL today announced the official launch of its first NING SERVICE Experience Center in Türkiye. The facility serves as the country's first dedicated battery depot repair center and integrated sales-and-service hub, marking a further step in expanding its localized new energy aftermarket service network and supporting the country's shift towards cleaner energy systems.

Türkiye sits at the crossroads of Europe, Asia and the Middle East — a regional economic hub with a fast-growing EV market and a rapidly expanding energy storage sector, where the shift toward clean energy is driving demand for specialized battery support. Its National Energy 2040 plan targets 20 million electric vehicles and 140 GWh of storage requirement by 2040. Against that backdrop, NING SERVICE is delivering full-lifecycle battery services on both the road and the grid, reinforcing the infrastructure that transition depends on.

Located in Istanbul, the NING SERVICE Experience Center represents an important milestone in the collaboration between CATL and Ascendum Türkiye, part of Ascendum Group, offering comprehensive full-lifecycle after-sales support, cultivating local technical talent and accelerating the deployment of advanced electrification and energy storage solutions.

Covering more than 1,200 square meters, the Istanbul center brings together service zones for battery testing, diagnosis, repair, maintenance and refurbishment, exhibition and retail space, training rooms and a customer lounge. The exhibition and retail area presents CATL's system-level capabilities across electric mobility and energy storage, including bedrock chassis, portable power stations, battery protection plates and integrated charging-and-storage units. The center serves as a localized service hub for the region and as a platform connecting partners across the ecosystem.

Providing a comprehensive new energy aftermarket service system

As CATL's independent aftermarket service brand, NING SERVICE delivers a one-stop, full-lifecycle battery service system that encompass battery diagnostics, repair, maintenance, refurbishment, training, recycling, aftermarket logistics and warehousing. Backed by CATL's deep R&D and extreme manufacturing capabilities, its services product categories from passenger and commercial vehicles to energy storage systems, setting a new benchmark for new energy service delivery in the region.

That capability is delivered through one of the industry's largest after-sales networks:

  • 1,429 professional service locations across more than 80 countries and regions, with the aim of reaching 100 countries and regions by 2027 and 10,000 service locations by 2030;
  • More than 9,900 service engineers and over 10,000 technicians certified for new energy after-sales service, with a 24-hour response mechanism in overseas markets;
  • Its deep-repair capability, delivered through a network of 95 centers, covers 76.8% of EV models and 90% of repair jobs;
  • The Intelligent Eagle Eye System, in use at more than 150 repair facilities, providing full traceability and quality control;
  • The Intelligent Battery Check System, supporting precise battery health diagnostics, slows battery aging by up to 9.5%;
  • More than 70 industry standards participated in or revised, and over 200 authorized patents worldwide

Strengthening local partnerships and service capabilities

CATL is extending its local footprint by strengthening infrastructure and building partnerships in the market. By combining CATL's technological expertise with Ascendum Group's 67 years of industrial heritage and robust local network, the Istanbul center enables CATL to serve clients throughout Türkiye, putting its know-how and rapid-response capability close to where batteries are actually in use.

The center anchors a network to all Türkiye and a team of CATL-certified engineers. It also serves as the network's training base, where technicians are trained and certified to CATL's standards before they work on customer batteries, building a local pool of battery service skills that the market will keep drawing on.

"The opening of Türkiye's first NING SERVICE Experience Center marks an important milestone in our strategic partnership with CATL and represents the first business initiative launched under Ascendum Green.Shift," said Tolga Polat, CEO of Ascendum Türkiye. "By combining CATL's advanced battery technologies with Ascendum's long-standing technical service expertise and customer-focused approach, we aim to provide reliable, high-quality aftermarket solutions across Türkiye. We are investing in local technical capabilities, developing specialized teams and strengthening our service infrastructure to meet the evolving needs of the energy and mobility sectors. Looking ahead, our goal is to gradually expand our service network nationwide and build a sustainable ecosystem that creates long-term value for our customers and supports Türkiye's energy transition."

"Türkiye has moved into the fast lane on electrification, and demand for aftermarket service will grow with it," said Bruce Li, Co-president of Sales & Marketing and President of Commercial Applications & Aftermarket Business of CATL. "As our first NING SERVICE Experience Center in the country, it brings CATL's technology, our training standards and Ascendum's local reach together, so that customers on the road and on the grid are served by people and parts that are already here. From here, we will keep extending our service network across Türkiye, work in step with the country's National Energy 2040 goals, and give the energy transition the service backbone it needs to hold up over time."

Looking ahead, NING SERVICE will continue to drive innovation in maintenance technology, service models and network expansion. The Istanbul center is the first step in Türkiye, with further network build-out and capability development to follow.

SOURCE CATL

data.title: Seek Loses Bull Amid Worries of Ad Volumes — Market Talk
data.description: Seek loses its bull at Jarden amid worries that job ad volumes could decline by more than the Australian employment marketplace expects. Analyst Nick Basile points out that unemployment rates are still lower than those seen pre-Covid and, with the economic backdrop deteriorating amid interest-rate rises and other pressures, he sees risk that volumes could be even weaker than the company anticipates. He thinks October's 6% decline is likely to be the best monthly figure of the December quarter. Jarden lowers its rating to neutral from overweight and cuts its target price on the stock 37% to 14.00 Australian dollars. Shares are down 5.2% at A$12.81. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)

data.title: LG Innotek Might Report Weaker 4Q Earnings — Market Talk
data.description: LG Innotek could report weaker 4Q earnings but still largely meet market expectations, says SK Kim at Daiwa Capital. The South Korea-based Apple supplier's optical-solutions division, which makes camera modules, faces pressure from higher prices for chip components and unfavorable foreign-exchange conditions, the analyst writes in a note. Kim expects the company's operating profit to fall 45% from a year earlier to 182 billion won in the Oct-Dec quarter, compared with the Bloomberg-consensus estimate of 188 billion won. For 2027, he expects iPhone camera upgrades to drive shipment growth for the company despite its limited ability to pass on higher costs to customers. Daiwa cuts the stock's target price by 65% to 325,000 won and keeps its outperform rating. Shares are 6.7% lower at 273,500 won.(kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)

data.title: Gold set for worst week since March as rate-hike expectations grow
data.description:
Gold prices eased on Friday and were headed for their steepest weekly decline since March, pressured by a resilient US dollar and growing expectations of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike next month, while investors parsed remarks from Fed officials for clues on the policy outlook.

FUNDAMENTALS

* Spot gold fell 0.4% to $3,607.47 per ounce by 0035 GMT, hitting its lowest level since early September 2025. Bullion was down about 7% so far for the week, its biggest weekly decline since March. US gold futures for December delivery slid 2.1% to $3,608.60.

* The dollar edged up on Thursday, extending its recent rally, that made greenback-priced bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies.

* The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits increased slightly last week, suggesting that labor market conditions remained stable, though some laid-off workers are struggling to find new opportunities.

* The booming rollout of artificial intelligence technology could strain the US economy's capacity and further boost inflation that the Fed will have to counteract, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday.

* Markets see a 97.3% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point move is priced at 2.7%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

* Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

* International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Thursday that energy supply shocks and Artificial Intelligence demand were accelerating global inflation to 4.7%, calling for a tightening of monetary policy in many economies.

* Elsewhere, Japan's annual core inflation accelerated in October and exceeded the central bank's 2% target for the second consecutive month, a sign of broadening price pressures.

* Meanwhile, Swiss gold exports fell to 109.7 metric tons in October, down 34% from the prior month as deliveries to Britain were lower, Swiss customs data showed on Thursday.

* Among other metals, spot silver was little changed at $42.74 per ounce, platinum fell 0.1% to $1,343.47, and palladium dipped 0.1% to $908.04. All three metals were headed for weekly losses.

data.title: BOJ's ambiguity on rate hike path could tempt yen bears
data.description:
Key points:
  • Hawks and doves split on how far BOJ should raise rates
  • No consensus on where neutral rate sits within estimated band
  • Rift may dilute BOJ's hawkish message, weigh on yen
  • December rate hike chance rising, next year's path less certain

By Leika Kihara

Bank of Japan policymakers mostly agree on the need for an interest rate hike next month, but their split over how far rates should eventually rise risks muddying the outlook and triggering a fresh round of yen selling.

BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda has struggled at times to get his hawkish signals across to markets, including in December last year, when the yen fell despite the decision then to hike rates.

While vague messaging helps the BOJ keep its options open amid heightened economic uncertainty, the lack of clarity on how far the bank could eventually raise rates has also become a particular trigger for yen bears.

A board reshuffle next year, which gives Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi a chance to replace two departing hawks with her preferred candidates, may also shift the debate around the terminal rate - now seen by markets at around 1.75% to 2%, analysts say.

That uncertainty could undermine any messages by Ueda that steady rate hikes were on the horizon as the bank focuses on mounting price pressures, analysts say.

"The BOJ may be hoping to avoid giving too clear a guidance on the pace of rate hikes, as it's their first experience seeking to anchor inflation around its 2% target," said Mari Iwashita, executive rates strategist at Nomura Securities.

"But sustained US rate hikes would keep the BOJ under pressure to raise rates too," in order to prevent US-Japan rate differentials from widening too much and triggering yen falls, she said.

AMBIGUITY DISCOUNT

Ueda last month declared inflation had reached the BOJ's 2% target and stressed a shift in phase towards policy that focuses on fighting inflation risks with steady rate hikes.

Speaking in parliament on Thursday, Ueda shrugged off recent soft signs in consumption as temporary and projected spending to recover, cementing the chance of a December rate hike.

What is less clear is the pace and timing of rate hikes next year with recent commentary from BOJ policymakers showing a divergence in their views on how far its policy rate - now at 1.25% - is from levels deemed neutral to the economy.

While BOJ staff estimates place Japan's nominal neutral rate in a range of 1.1% to 2.5%, there is no consensus within the board on where within the band the neutral rate lies.

Hawkish board member Naoki Tamura projected the neutral rate to be around 2%. Another hawk, Hajime Takata, said on Monday the BOJ must raise rates to a "good" position, which he described as near the middle of the estimated 1.1%-2.5% range.

Others seen by markets as holding the casting vote on the rate-hike timing are less sure. Former academic Junko Koeda has said only the neutral rate was "likely significantly above 1%."

Kazuyuki Masu has not given any projection on the neutral rate but stressed in September the need to pull real interest rates out of negative territory as soon as possible.

Doves, on the other hand, see less scope for further hikes, signalling the policy rate may already be close to neutral.

Toichiro Asada said last week Japan's neutral rate was "not necessarily high," while Ayano Sato cited weak consumption as a reason for voting against the September hike.

YEN HOLDS KEY

A majority of economists polled by Reuters expect the BOJ to raise rates to 1.5% in December, followed by another hike by end-March. They see the terminal rate to be around 1.75% or 2%.

Ueda and his two deputies have done little to give markets clarity, staying mum on the neutral level and saying only that loose financial conditions leave scope for continued rate hikes.

The ambiguity reflects the difficulty predicting how households and firms, accustomed to prolonged ultra-low rates, react to steadily rising borrowing costs.

Even the hawks have held off on proposing aggressive tightening measures. Takata, for one, said the BOJ must avoid being bound by particular intervals in raising rates and take a nimble, data-dependent approach.

Some lawmakers who grilled Ueda in parliament on Thursday questioned his view that consumption will recover, a sign of the political heat the BOJ may face in steering further rate hikes.

While Takaichi has said little on the BOJ's rate-hike plans, she will have the chance to fill openings in the nine-member board when the two hawks, Tamura and Takata, see their terms expire in July next year.

The seat now occupied by former banker Tamura may go to a conservative megabank executive, however, the other opening may be filled by a candidate less hawkish than Takata, analysts say.

In the end, yen moves will be key to how far the BOJ will raise rates, said veteran BOJ watcher Katsutoshi Inadome, who projects rates to move up to 2.0% next year - or even to 2.25% around the summer if the yen continues to weaken.

"Given so many moving parts, maybe it's inevitable the BOJ's message becomes ambiguous," said Inadome, who is senior strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset ​Management.

"But if the yen's weakness persists, the BOJ will have little choice but to keep hiking steadily. I also wonder whether Takaichi would do anything that would push down the yen."

data.title: Trump's Personal Lawyer to Step Down as Sullivan & Cromwell Co-Chair — WSJ
data.description:
By Erin Mulvaney

Sullivan & Cromwell co-chair Robert Giuffra, who broke from other elite lawyers when he decided to represent President Trump, is stepping down from firm leadership.

Both of the firm's chairs — Giuffra, a respected litigator, and corporate lawyer Scott Miller — are stepping aside for new leadership. The pair had co-led the firm since 2022. They will be succeeded by Carsten Berrar and Sharon Nelles, who will take the reins in January 2028.

It isn't uncommon for large law firms to announce succession plans a year or more in advance. Sullivan & Cromwell doesn't have prescribed term limits for its chairs, but has a policy that lawyers leave the leadership role after turning 65.

Giuffra will be 67 years old next year, and Miller will be 66. Both will continue doing client work at the firm.

Sullivan & Cromwell is a 147-year-old New York firm with roughly 900 lawyers that attracts Ivy League graduates and represents some of the nation's biggest corporations.

Giuffra is a veteran trial lawyer known for representing major corporations such as Volkswagen and Goldman Sachs. He recently won an appeal for Argentina, reversing a $16 billion judgment tied to the nationalization of oil company YPF as part of long-running litigation.

Giuffra agreed after the 2024 election to represent Trump in two New York appeals, including his conviction in the Stormy Daniels hush-money case. He had also been under consideration to run the Justice Department.

Giuffra's decision to represent Trump has drawn controversy inside and outside his firm. Partners bristled about not being consulted about him taking on the Trump cases when many larger firms still eschewed working for him.

"Sullivan & Cromwell's decision to represent President Trump was undertaken following thorough discussion with our firm's nearly 200 partners, and deliberation at our Managing Partners Committee and Management Committee," a firm spokesman said.

Giuffra also has advised the president, including helping broker a deal for Trump to drop an executive order targeting rival law firm Paul Weiss last year. That set off a series of similar deals.

Democratic lawmakers have pressed Giuffra to disclose his role in the deals. With the party poised to take control of Congress early next year, lawmakers sent letters this week asking the dealmaking law firms, including Kirkland & Ellis, Skadden Arps, and Simpson Thacher, to disclose information about work done for the government.

Nelles will be the first woman to hold the chair role at Sullivan & Cromwell. She has worked with clients including Volkswagen, JPMorgan, Moody's, Airbnb, Boeing, Goldman Sachs, and Microsoft.

Berrar, who runs the firm's Frankfurt office and helps lead its capital-markets practice, will be the first chair of the firm not based in the U.S. He has advised Delivery Hero on its sale to Uber, as well as Porsche and Zalando.

Write to Erin Mulvaney at erin.mulvaney@wsj.com

data.title: Marimaca Hits Broad Copper-Silver Zones at Pampa Medina Deposit in Chile
data.description:
Marimaca Copper has reported further high-grade copper and silver intersections at its Pampa Medina deposit in northern Chile, strengthening evidence of mineralisation continuity ahead of an initial resource estimate.

The standout result was 102 metres grading 1.00% copper and 5.1 grams per tonne silver, intersected from a downhole depth of 706m in the central zone.

Another hole 150m farther north returned 68m at 1.13% copper and 8.7g/t silver, including a higher-grade 22m section at 2.07% copper and 10.0g/t silver.

The drilling is testing stacked mineralised layers at Pampa Medina, approximately 28 kilometres east of the company’s Marimaca oxide deposit in Chile’s Antofagasta Region.

Central Zone Reinforces Continuity

Drill holes spaced about 150m apart have intersected copper-bearing sulphide layers across the central high-grade zone, supporting Marimaca’s interpretation of a connected mineralised system.

Within the broad 102m intersection, assays included 72m grading 1.24% copper and 6.8g/t silver, with a 14m interval returning 1.80% copper and 10.4g/t silver.

Other central-zone drilling intersected 34m at 1.36% copper and 6.6g/t silver, including 18m at 2.07% copper and 12.4g/t silver deeper in the target sedimentary sequence.

A separate hole encountered several mineralised layers, including 18m at 1.69% copper and 13.3g/t silver with an 8m section grading 3.21% copper and 27.5g/t silver.

Expanded Oxide Footprint

The program has also identified oxide mineralisation outside the previously mapped shallow deposit alongside further sulphide intersections to the south.

One hole returned 84m grading 0.62% copper and 3.2g/t silver in an oxide zone, including 46m at 1.06% copper and 6.0g/t silver.

That intersection was drilled about 300m west of the historical oxide footprint, while another hole extended the recognised oxide mineralisation roughly 150m west.

In the northern part of the deposit, drilling returned 54m at 1.12% copper and 9.9g/t silver, reinforcing earlier results in the same area.

Some deeper drilling was interrupted by late intrusive dykes, leaving parts of the targeted mineralised horizons untested.

Ongoing Resource Work

Marimaca is nearing completion of central-zone drilling within a defined area measuring approximately 3km by 1.5km, with the results intended to support a maiden mineral resource estimate.

“We are nearing completion of the central-zone drilling that will support our maiden resource estimate, while also extending mineralisation beyond the historical oxide footprint,” vice president of exploration Sergio Rivera said.

“Pampa Medina is part of a much larger land package, and we believe there is meaningful exploration potential beyond the area drilled to date.”

The company plans to move drilling north and west of the present deposit towards the Pampa Norte and Sierra Norte targets that sit within the broader Sierra de Medina land package, where geophysical work has identified prospective sedimentary horizons beyond the area drilled to date.

data.title: Northrop forgoes challenge to Boeing’s $20B+ Navy fighter win
data.description:
Northrop Grumman won't challenge the Navy’s selection of Boeing for the F/A-XX stealth fighter program, Bloomberg News reported, removing a potential obstacle to development under a contract valued at more than $20 billion.

For investors, the decision reduces the risk of a protest-related delay to a major Boeing defense program. The award adds to Boeing’s success in securing the Air Force’s F-47 fighter contract in 2025, strengthening its position in next-generation military aviation.

Northrop said it reached its decision after reviewing information and receiving a Navy debriefing. A challenge before the Government Accountability Office could have delayed the program for months while the agency considered the dispute.

Defense consultant JJ Gentler suggested Northrop may have accepted the Navy’s explanation or prioritized its other Pentagon commitments. Those include the Sentinel nuclear missile program, with an expected cost exceeding $141 billion, and the B-21 bomber.

data.title: Australia Inflation Data Likely to Highlight RBA's Dilemma — Market Talk
data.description: Australia's October monthly inflation data due on Wednesday will be the critical event Down Under next week. The market anticipates a monthly gain in the trimmed mean CPI of 0.3%, which would see annual trimmed mean inflation ease to 3.5% from 3.6%, says David Bassanese, chief economist at Betashares. But after Thursday's weak jobs data, even an absolute shocker of an inflation result seems unlikely to force the Reserve Bank of Australia to hike rates in December, he adds. A hot inflation print would only add to the dilemma facing the economy and the RBA - namely slowing economic growth but still sticky inflation, he adds. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

We are investing in local technical capabilities, developing specialized teams and strengthening our service infrastructure to meet the evolving needs of the energy and mobility sectors. Looking ahead, our goal is to gradually expand our service network nationwide and build a sustainable ecosystem that creates long-term value for our customers and supports Türkiye's energy transition."

"Türkiye has moved into the fast lane on electrification, and demand for aftermarket service will grow with it," said Bruce Li, Co-president of Sales & Marketing and President of Commercial Applications & Aftermarket Business of CATL. "As our first NING SERVICE Experience Center in the country, it brings CATL's technology, our training standards and Ascendum's local reach together, so that customers on the road and on the grid are served by people and parts that are already here. From here, we will keep extending our service network across Türkiye, work in step with the country's National Energy 2040 goals, and give the energy transition the service backbone it needs to hold up over time."

Looking ahead, NING SERVICE will continue to drive innovation in maintenance technology, service models and network expansion. The Istanbul center is the first step in Türkiye, with further network build-out and capability development to follow.

data.title: Accused child sex predator Thomas Markle ruled competent to face trial
data.description:
A U.S. judge in Florida on Thursday declared Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Britain's Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Markle, to be mentally competent to answer to a federal charge filed in court earlier this month accusing him of being a child sexual predator.

Agreeing with the findings of a court-appointed forensic psychiatrist, US Magistrate Judge Lindsay Griffin ruled that the 82-year-old father-in-law of Prince Harry was mentally fit to understand the proceedings against him and to properly assist in his own defense.

He was charged November 5 in a criminal complaint with a single felony count of possessing child sexual abuse images.

According to an FBI affidavit filed with the complaint, the material in question, including two explicit photos of Markle posed with a naked underage girl and other images of him with children in various stages of undress, was found in two Los Angeles storage units.

Commenting on the case at the time of his arrest on November 6 at an assisted-living center in Florida, FBI Director ​Kash Patel said Markle had "targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions."

data.title: Asian gasoline margin plunges to over three-year lows on ample supplies
data.description:
By Mohi Narayan

Asian gasoline margins plummeted around 69% this week as abundant supplies from China and the Middle East weighed on crack spreads, traders and analysts said on Thursday.

The refining profit, or crack, (GL92-SIN-CRK) for gasoline shrank to $2.67 per barrel over Brent crude, the lowest level since October 2023, from a record peak of $50.53 on October 1.

"Increased Chinese exports are further weighing on the sentiment," Stuti Jhunjhunwala, oil market analyst at Energy Aspects, said.

Gasoline crack spreads usually shrink heading into the northern hemisphere's winter, when fuel demand falls, however, this year they hit record highs on a tight supply outlook, caused by the Middle East war, Russia's export ban and lower inventories at key trading hubs.

The margins fell to six-month lows at the end of October and have been on a downward trend since amid hopes of higher supplies.

"Plenty of supplies from China and year-end destocking causing the fall," a Dubai-based light distillate trader said.

Meanwhile, gasoline imports at the Singapore trading and blending hub tanked 69% to 67,000 tons (about 566,000 barrels) in the week to November 18, while exports rose about 13% on-week to roughly 459,000 tons, government data showed.

The top supplier was China at about 50,000 tons, while the top destination for exports was Australia at 111,000 tons.
